captures.notes: This seed produces a different taller construction signature with thirteen connected stacks. Light planks, pitched caps, and staggered masses remain consistent without looking like palette-only variation.
The reverse overview shows a tightly interlocked roofline and several distinct base heights; visible terrain is confined to the outer edge rather than forming a central vertical hole.
The east section verifies roof closure on the long and tower families, no frontage-wider-than-depth hut, and structural surfaces supported to their declared datum.
The entrance is a furnished market alley bounded by stalls and inhabited facades. Its two-turn shape prevents a sightline through to the opposite side.
Although this seed has the corpus's lowest overhead ratio, the hostile reverse route is still visually enclosed by nearby facades, stocked market pieces, and a turning public surface.
The cross-route view terminates in built mass and a change of direction instead of exposing a lawn corridor through the city.
The elevated route is continuous at doors and transitions, uses authored light boards, and derives its guard openings from the same threshold and stair seams.
The roofed occupied connection is visibly attached to both endpoint buildings; surrounding roof mass creates intentional compression without hiding an open seam.
The underside view confirms exterior air below inhabited mass and a bounded passage rather than an unsupported dark platform.
The complete skyline has pitched repeat runs and sealed ends on rooms, bays, and links; no room wall rises into an absent roof.
The network view shows a different maze and parcel arrangement from seed 0, one bounded lightwell, and no large uncovered core component.
